title: Sweet and Tangy Beef and Bean Spaghetti
changes_from_base: A one-pot family supper: beef mince, two kinds of beans and a sweet-tangy ketchup and vinegar sauce replace the plain tomato sauce, finished with Cheddar.
summary: A hearty one-pot spaghetti with beef mince, kidney and black beans and a sweet-tangy tomato sauce, finished with melting Cheddar.
equipment: large flameproof casserole or deep pan

ingredients.item: dried spaghetti, broken into 8 cm lengths
fine salt for 2 litres of pasta water (0.5%)
ingredients.note: about 1.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: tinned chopped tomatoes (no salt added), drained
tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed
tin black beans (no salt added), drained and rinsed
mature Cheddar, grated, plus extra to serve

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the broken spaghetti in 2 litres salted water, stirring often, until al dente. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well so it does not stick while you make the sauce.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium heat and cook most of the onion for 4-5 min until soft but not brown, then add the garlic for 30 s.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Add the mince with the pepper and break it into small pieces with the spoon. Cook about 5 min until no pink remains and the meat reaches 71 °C.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in the tomatoes, both beans, ketchup, chilli powder and vinegar. The ketchup gives the sweet base and the vinegar the tang. Add the spaghetti and heat through for about 5 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the Cheddar until melted. Serve with extra cheese and the reserved raw onion.

tips: Breaking the spaghetti makes it easy to eat with a spoon and stops it clumping.
Rinse the cooked pasta so it does not turn gummy while it waits.
Swap the chilli powder for chipotle for a smokier pot.
storage: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C).
